Help with terminology! What is it called when you sue someone [...]

Won or lost a lawsuit

Or had it thrown out
Is "had it thrown out" the same thing as losing? Or is "throwing out" abandoning it?

The judge dismisses it before any hearing.

Different than losing after a hearing.

Thrown out is when the judge deems the case invalid and not worth being heard in court. It is what SHOULD happen if I punched you for no reason and then sued for damages to my hand, the judge says that I have no case and dismisses it or in out of court speak throws it out.
Not winning could be a dismissal or settlement. Winning is a default judgement for plantiff.

IANAL

you can win BY default, but every judgment doesn't have to be a default judgment. winning by default usually means that one party did not appear, either in person or by submitting court ordered papers, and the court has decided against the party who did not appear.

dismissal usually means that the judge ended the case, for any number of reasons. a judge can dismiss a case at any time, before or after hearings are held. a defendant (the person being sued) can specifically ask a judge to dismiss a case at any number of points during that case.

discontinued usually means that the plaintiff (the one suing) has withdrawn or requested the case be closed before any decision or settlement is reached. this is generally good for the defendant because the plaintiff is saying 'nope, don't want this lawsuit to continue, bye.' 'discontinuances' as documents can be filed with the court after the proceedings to officially close the case, irrespective of any decision or settlement.

settlement is an agreement between the parties for one or both sides to do and/or get something. this happens before a case is decided. as a defendant, a settlement can be a good thing because at some level, you're not being held liable for something you've been sued for. settlements can be good for plaintiffs as well, because sometimes you have to take a gamble that the settlement will be more favorable than what the judge's decision will be.

a judge's decision in favor of someone can be called an 'award', as in 'the judge awarded me $1000 dollars in my suit'.

You have to check the Settings for everything that you download. Uninstall all apps that you don't use and check the privacy settings on all of the ones you keep ( this goes for your phone, too). If you use things like Ghostery go in and uncheck the box that enables them to send data. It's a pain, but it has to be our new habit. They all do unless you uncheck the boxes.
